newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. extends Iraq no-fly zone. [CORRECTED 13:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. extends Iraq no-fly zone. [CORRECTED 13:07 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday the United States was extending the no-fly zone in southern (corrects from northern) Iraq to Baghdad's southern suburbs and taking other steps in retaliation for Iraq's military move against Kurds.

"First, we are extending the no-fly zone in southern Iraq. This will deny Saddam control of Iraqi air space from the Kuwaiti border to the southern suburbs of Baghdad," Clinton said in his statement from the Oval Office. "It significantly restricts Iraq's ability to conduct offensive operations."

In what was his first public comment on an overnight U.S. cruise missile strike against Iraq, he also said a United Nations plan to allow Iraq to sell oil to raise hard currency for purchases of food and medicines could not proceed under the current circumstances.

The U.S. missile attack was prompted by the decision of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein to send troops across the 36th parallel defining a no-fly zone that allied forces imposed around Kurdish areas of northern Iraq after the 1991 Gulf War. The Iraqis occupied the Kurdish town of Erbil and Clinton said there was no sign they had withdrawn from that area.

"We must make it clear that reckless acts have consequences or those acts will increase," he said. "... Our objectives are limited but clear: to make Saddam pay a price for the latest act of brutality, reducing his ability to threaten his neighbors and America's interests."
